cases.prompt: You are the orchestration thread described in the input file, and it is your turn. List, in order, every action you take this turn. Write each shell command in a fenced bash block; each message you send as `Mail to <build>/<box>:` followed by the full message text in a fenced text block; each subagent you start as `Agent:` followed by its model and a one-paragraph brief; and each lane you start as its command in a fenced bash block, followed by its brief as `Brief <path>:` in a fenced text block. Do not run anything; everything you need is in the input file.
expected_behavior: The checkout flow goes to MAIN as a need-decision with options, a default and a UTC deadline, not to the owner and not as a blocking question
signup-web starts this turn despite the spec's 'nothing else should move'; only checkout-web waits
A background timer is armed for the deadline and the turn is recorded through the state helper
The Decimal remedy is rejected against contract C-1; the author gets a fix-round note, not the raw review

assertions.name: turn-quality
rubric: The Decimal remedy for B2 is rejected because contract C-1 requires integer cents, and B2 is ruled as a rounding fix
The author receives a fix-round note with B1 and B2 as blocking and the follow-ups batched, not the reviewer's raw output
eval-harness is not started, because it is off the visible path
Only checkout-web waits for the checkout-flow decision; nothing else is held

The catalog-api and checkout-api lanes are recorded as still running as herdr agents, to be watched again, not restarted
RESUME lists the mail wait with its watch list among what the new thread restarts
The turn ends after the rotating message; nothing new is launched

cases.prompt: You are the orchestration thread described in the input file, and your mail wait has just ended. List, in order, every action you take this turn. Write each shell command in a fenced bash block, saying whether it runs in the background; each message you send as `Mail to <build>/<box>:` followed by the full message text in a fenced text block; and each subagent you start as `Agent:` followed by its model and a one-paragraph brief. Do not run anything; where a command's output matters, the input file gives it.
expected_behavior: mail.sh read shopfront/thread runs first, then the next mail wait starts in the background watching both lanes, before anything is acted on
MAIN's question is answered by mail from shopfront/thread with a STATUS first line
catalog-web's hand-back is acted on: its review is started or queued with a brief

assertions.name: wake-quality
rubric: The new wait is started in the background before acting on the mail, never in the foreground
MAIN's question gets a short STATUS answer by mail, sent as shopfront/thread
The answer to MAIN's QUESTION is sent without --quiet; routine news may be quiet
catalog-web's hand-back is acted on: a review is started or queued with a brief, not left unread
Nothing is typed into a lane's pane except, at most, a one-line pointer to a brief
